# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (for later Q&A; replaces the source text)

## BOOK 1 of 2: SETTLING DAY (Nat Gould; Gutenberg 35496; Australian bush, c. 1890s)

**Front matter:** Other Gould titles: Sporting Sketches, A Racecourse Tragedy, Warned Off, The Double Event. Publisher R.A. Everett & Co., 42 Essex Street, Strand. Chapters I–XXX.

**Ch I "The Little Chap":** Jim Dennis rides mare Bess hard from Wanabeen to Swamp Creek to fetch Dr Tom for son Willie (six years old) who is dying of fever. Wanabeen = Jim's lonely station, New South Wales. Dr Thomas Sheridan ("Dr Tom"): ex-ship's surgeon, drinks, big-hearted, idolised, never refuses a call. Dr Tom sees Jim, drives buggy with pair (ill-kept rig). One horse goes down, Jim forces it up. Arrive; Dr Tom saves boy: "Come in, Jim, the little chap's alive." Jim: "Thank God!"

**Ch II "Black Sal":** Wanabeen description (galvanised iron, white ants, five steps). Sal = half-caste, ~25, brought up on mission, escaped; once of King Charlie's tribe (King Charlie wears metal half-moon plate, "order of the garter"; cursed Sal). Sal collapsed at Wanabeen steps ~3 years earlier; Jim carried her in, took her in. Willie then 3 yrs old ("Pitty woman"). Sal devoted to Willie, dog-like devotion to Jim. Dr Tom: "Jim, where is the lad's mother?" Jim: "Settling Day."

**Ch III "Potter's Shanty":** Robbery of mail coach at Potter's Shanty (Samuel "Old Sam" Potter, illiterate, ex-Kelly gang, acquitted of forgery by "what's a bill?"). Bank agent (Nation's Bank, Swamp Creek branch manager) robbed; £5 note traced to Jim who cashed it at Swamp Creek Hotel; suspicion on Jim, police Sergeant Machinson (Barragong, 10 miles away) hostile. Coach driver Ned Glenn (old, weathered, merry eyes, pictured in Sydney Lantern as Claude Duval) is Jim's friend; sides with Jim. Ned: "hope to see him on the back of a cup winner for his dad." Dr Tom asks Jim "Who put it up?" – Jim angry.

**Ch IV "Jim's Trouble":** Backstory: wife Maud Dennis (city-bred) left Jim with infant Willie to go to Sydney; left on Ned Glenn's coach; never returned. Her father wrote Maud left a week before; she claimed Jim was bad and that Willie was not hers. Jim swore vengeance: "settling day." Jim refuses to let Willie learn mother's name. Jim is a superb horseman who breaks in buck-jumpers. Dr Tom's bought horse broken by Jim. Jim sees Willie as future jockey. Willie: "I mean to be as good a rider as you are."

**Ch V "A Regular Savage":** Storm breaks drought. Strange stallion (thoroughbred, later "Seahorse") joins Jim's mob; Jim fights it with stock-whip; Constable Fred Doonan (Jim's friend, stationed at Swamp Creek) rescues him. Doonan mentions Rodney Shaw returned from England.

**Ch VI "Rodney Shaw":** Wealthiest squatter; station Cudgegong (~30–40 sq miles); away ~7–8 years; shifty, half-frightened, changed. Manager Benjamin Nix. Jim rides to Cudgegong (15 miles), meets Sergeant Machinson, who suspects him. Rodney Shaw cold, says horse was stolen from Potter's (man in charge Alec Beg).

**Ch VII "Outwitted":** Jim distrusts Shaw. Sal reports two men came for horse (Dalton's gang). Jim pursues to Barker's Creek (gang HQ; Abe Dalton's gang; blacks of King Charlie's tribe cast off). Jim catches the men at dusk, takes stallion back, bluffs with six-chambered revolver. Takes horse to Cudgegong, sleeps on verandah.

**Ch VIII "At Cudgegong Station":** Shaw awake, drunk-ish, startled; amnesia claim ("hurdle race fall"). Jim mentions Adye Dauntsey (police magistrate, Barragong); Shaw writes "Adye" on chair. Alec Beg (hand) dislikes Jim. Stallion named Seahorse (by Fisherman out of Mermaid). Jim offers mares to Seahorse. Shaw's inner thoughts: wants Sal; "that lady friend" in London.

**Ch IX "The Sort of Man Dr Tom Is":** Dr Tom's poem rejected by ship's skipper (fiery beard); published in Morning Light via shipping reporter bribed with whisky. Dr Tom borrowed from Jim. Baalim (dog, ugly, dingo/kangaroo-dog mix). Doonan tells Dr Tom of attack plan; Dr Tom vows to face Dalton.

**Ch X "A Frightened Scoundrel":** Dr Tom goes to Barker's Creek (black boy aged ~40). Dalton sick (fever); Dr Tom frightens him, Dalton swears not to molest Jim or property; Dr Tom saves him. Gang member says Machinson takes bribes from Dalton. Dr Tom stays a day and night.

**Ch XI "'Try Willie'":** Willie 12, fine rider. Shaw covets Sal; offers money; Jim refuses coldly. Swamp Creek Cup (£200 + silver cup); Shaw gave half stake. Jim's grey colt Neptune (by Seahorse, dam La Perouse), sixteen hands. Jim doubts Ben Madsley's temper. Dr Tom: "Try Willie." Dr Tom is race secretary/starter.

**Ch XII "Mainly Concerning a Dog":** Dr Tom's dog Baalim. Dr Tom's violin, "Ode to Spring." Jim sets Willie on Neptune. Dr Tom's "drifted" confession. Dr Tom owes money; Alf Sniggers offers bullock payment.

**Ch XIII "Speculation":** Bookmaker Aaron Hyam (Gum Tree Hotel; son Moses). First Class favourite (Bourke). Shaw's Seahorse colts Distant Shore and Seaweed; jockey Ben Madsley on Distant Shore. Abe Dalton's The Captain (jockey Jackson). Dalton v Dr Tom bet at Gum Tree: Dr Tom bets £20 on Neptune; Dalton calls Willie a "half-caste" and "brat"; Dr Tom flings Dalton off bar. Dr Tom says winnings to Bathurst Hospital.

**Ch XIV "The Half-Caste's Warning":** Ned Glenn tells Jim Dr Tom saved Dalton and made deal. Jim wants to tell Willie; spits; Sal weeps. Sal: King Charlie's curse on her; warns Rodney Shaw is "your enemy", he tempted her, wants her. "Abe Dalton says" Willie is Sal's child.

**Ch XV "A Cowardly Assault":** Yellow jacket for Willie (from Sydney via Ned Glenn). Jim and Willie at Gum Tree. Shaw bets Jim £100 to £50 Distant Shore beats Neptune. Dalton, while Dr Tom and Jim at the hotel, creeps to Dr Tom's house, strikes sleeping Willie on head with pestle. Dalton meets Doonan. Dalton and Shaw deal: Shaw pays £100 to kidnap Sal; Dalton ("blackbirding"). Willie concussed.

**Ch XVI "The Morning of the Race":** Willie recovers; Adye Dauntsey (friend of Dr Tom, P.M.) arrives. Dalton bets Aaron Hyam. Dauntsey says he'll instruct Machinson. Jim says Seth Sharp (murderer, freed after 15 years) is at Barker's Creek. Shaw visits; Willie says "first race". Shaw notes Willie is plucky.

**Ch XVII "At the Post":** Course a mile round, ran twice. Fourteen runners. Jackson (The Captain) foul-prone. Jim's instructions to Willie. Dr Tom starter fines Jackson. Neptune hard to start.

**Ch XVIII "His First Race":** Neptune breaks, Shaw's Seaweed pacemaker; Willie goes wide. Willie's head swims from blow. Final: Neptune vs Distant Shore; judge's verdict short head to Neptune. Jim bets Shaw £50 Neptune beats Distant Shore; Aaron Hyam takes other £50. Dr Tom: "Neptune's won!"

**Ch XIX "Sal at Work":** Willie weighs in, faints. Dr Tom publicly accuses Dalton. Sergeant Machinson dismisses. Rodney Shaw meets Sal; she thanks. Shaw: "I'll have her." Sal to Doonan: suspects Dalton. Sal confronts Dalton: "King Charlie is not yet dead... Barker's Creek will run with blood."

**Ch XX "Danger at Hand":** Jim and Dr Tom ride to Barragong to visit Dauntsey. Gin from Barker's Creek warns Sal. Silas Dixon (surly hand) sent for Doonan. Willie rides to find Doonan near Barker's Creek. Doonan: Ned Glenn shot dead by Seth Sharp during coach robbery 3 miles outside Swamp Creek; Dalton's men implicated.

**Ch XXI "A Clever Escape":** Dalton's men ambush at Wanabeen hut; kill black gin (shot through head with Sal's revolver). Sal captured, strapped on horse, taken to Cudgegong. Shaw pays Dalton £100 +£20 extra. Sal chains? No: locked in room; escapes through floor (white ants weakened skirting board), runs, sleeps exhausted.

**Ch XXII "Determined Men":** Doonan, Silas, Willie find gin dead. Doonan finds Sal; takes her home. Adye Dauntsey, Machinson and six police arrive. Machinson apologises to Jim. Council of war. Plan: attack Barker's Creek at night.

**Ch XXIII "The Attack on Barker's Creek":** King Charlie (with tribe from Woolloola, >100) advances; Sal had sent him (he saw her mound grave). Machinson's men attacked; Jim sets bush fire; Jim and Doonan go to meet King Charlie's tribe.

**Ch XXIV "A Fierce Fight":** Blacks attack rear; Dalton's men fight. Shaw escapes on horse; Doonan shoots him (wound between shoulders). Jim wounded in arm. Dalton shoots Machinson dead; Dauntsey shoots Dalton's hand. Seth Sharp captured. Dalton and five others taken alive; ten gang killed. Barker's Creek burned.

**Ch XXV "A Stricken Woman":** Dr Tom reports to press. A week later Maud Dennis (Willie's mother, Jim's ex-wife) arrives at Wanabeen half-dead; collapses on steps. Sal wakes Jim; Jim intends to kill her, Sal stops him. Maud confesses Rodney Shaw took her to London/Sydney; she was with Shaw. Jim vows "Settling day" with Shaw. Maud dies later in Dr Tom's presence with Willie holding her hand.

**Ch XXVI "Settling Day":** Jim rides to Cudgegong. Shaw is wounded, feverish; Jim cannot strike wounded man; Shaw bleeds, dies. Jim: "He will have a heavy settling day." Nix: "Sometimes I have thought he was not Rodney Shaw."

**Ch XXVII "Neptune's Son":** Barker's Creek gang tried at Bathurst; all sentenced to death. Doonan promoted sergeant. Chris Shaw (cousin) inherits Cudgegong; offers Jim management, later sale. Grey Bird (four-year-old, by Neptune out of Seamew) entered in Sydney Cup; Jim and Dr Tom and Willie go to Sydney. Sergeant Doonan bets £5.

**Ch XXVIII "Grey Bird is Admired":** Randwick; Grey Bird 100–3 odds, Jim bets £1,000 to £30 twice (≈£12,000 win). Dr Tom backs £500. Defiance (Jack Ashton), Target (Chris Shaw's; jockey Hurley). Molly Corbold (cousin of Dauntsey) meets Jim. Chris Shaw promises Cudgegong for £12,000 cash if Grey Bird wins. Ashton rough: "country-bred imp."

**Ch XXIX "A Glorious Victory":** Tatters led early. Willie squeezes through. Ashton boring; Willie's left stirrup leather breaks; he recovers. Final: Grey Bird wins by a neck from Bung Bung, Defiance a head third. Scale won't go down; bridle fetched; weighs in. Willie: "What about the up-country imp now?"

**Ch XXX "In the Days of Prosperity":** Five years later. Grey Bird now stud at Cudgegong. Jim paid £12,000 for Cudgegong; Wanabeen also his. Sal married Sergeant Doonan. Jim marries Molly Corbold (Adye Dauntsey's cousin; housekeeper, Dauntsey's household). Swamp Creek gold rush township; Dr Tom prosperous, new house, poetry obsession. Willie refuses to ride for others. Closing: Jim on verandah at Cudgegong; "autumn of his life was full of peace."

---

## BOOK 2 of 2: THE RUNAWAYS (Nat Gould; Gutenberg 39631; English hunting/racing, c. 1900s)

**Ch I "As the Snow Falls":** Redmond Maynard, Squire of Hazelwell (Irene's guardian), stands at dining-room window on anniversary (two years) of son Ulick's departure after quarrel. Dog Bersak (wolf-hound; once saved Ulick from bull). Irene Courtly (née Carstone, daughter of late Colonel Carstone), married to Warren Courtly of Anselm Manor, arrives on foot; Warren "gone to London". Bob Heather (groom) fetches maid Mary Marley. Squire: "Warren is an ass." Irene sits at Squire's feet. Ulick's father's words: "Believing... that I am guilty... I will no longer inflict my presence upon you, sir."

**Ch II "The Runaways":** Eli Todd, stud manager, ex-Colonel Carstone's man (Hussars, India). Daughter Janet Todd eloped same night as Ulick two years ago; Eli believes Ulick innocent. Squire accused Ulick of ruining Janet. Mrs Marley housekeeper. Bob Heather visits Eli for ale; tells him Irene's situation.

**Ch III "Random":** Bersak guards Squire. Squire sees hare/fox. Random = bay hunter formerly Ulick's; given to Irene; Irene's painting of Random. Warren jealous of horse; wants it sold. Irene's Anselm Manor history (Henry VIII deed). Irene married Warren ~6 months after Ulick left.

**Ch IV "Irene's Painting":** Irene rides Rupert to Anselm Manor; Eli on way; Honeysuckle (old mare, heavy in foal). Warren's letter (et cetera, scented paper). Letter from Felix Hoffman (Feltham, Middlesex) begging money; Irene sends £5. Housekeeper Martha Dixon.

**Ch V "Honeysuckle's Foal":** New Year's Eve; colt foal born quarter hour after midnight. Ulick secretly visits Eli in stable; says he has the Saint (racehorse, grey, by Father Confessor out of Hilda, race name Mr Lanark). Ulick says he never wronged Janet.

**Ch VI "A Wily Young Man":** Felix Hoffman, Jewish-looking, 25, racecourse tout; mother Mrs Hoffman (Feltham). Warren met Felix at Hurst Park (Milander). Warren placed Janet at Mrs Hoffman's as "Mrs Warren" (£3 guineas/week).

**Ch VII "Selling His Heritage":** Felix reads Warren's letter; writes to Irene. Warren sold Holme Farm for £10,000 to pay debts. Janet demands money. Squire: Holme Farm worth £5,000 more.

**Ch VIII "Warren's Return":** Warren confesses sale to Irene; Felix's letter returning £5. Warren visits Squire; Squire forgives Ulick, wants Irene protected. Warren sees Felix's letter; Felix threatens.

**Ch IX "How Ulick Bought the Saint":** Ulick in London (West Kensington flat); Christmas in London; gives 10 shillings to homeless children. Fred May (Squire's old trainer) sells him the Saint for 200 guineas (owner disliked grey colour).

**Ch X "The Curiosity":** Saint wins Pastures Handicap at Kempton over Pinkerton (jockey Ben Sprig, olive green jacket, owner Mr Lanark); Kit Cat (Conrad Rush) second, Pinkerton second. Ulick sees Janet in Feltham.

**Ch XI "For a Woman's Sake":** Ulick visits Janet at Mrs Hoffman's (Feltham); Warren arrives, Janet hides Ulick. Warren's quarrel with Janet over money. Ulick realises Warren is the seducer; sworn to keep Irene from knowing.

**Ch XII "Two Schemers":** Dr Harding (doctor) urges Squire change of air. Eli writes to Ulick. Fred May and Eli arrange reconciliation at Newmarket (Stanton House). Squire and Ulick reconcile; Ulick refuses to return until "reasons" resolved.

**Ch XIII "The Squire and the Saint":** Squire sees the Saint ("dirty grey"). Dinner at Walton Hotel with Warren and Irene. Ulick and Irene on balcony; Irene admits she never believed him guilty.

**Ch XIV "A Discovery Imminent":** Warren pays Felix £50 blackmail. Felix's letter to Irene: names Mrs Warren at Feltham; demands £100. Irene travels to Feltham.

**Ch XV "The Result of the Discovery":** Irene confronts Janet at Feltham; Janet confesses. Irene urges Janet to return home; Janet refuses (promised Ulick). Warren rages at Walton; Irene invites Ulick to dinner.

**Ch XVI "A Race to Be Remembered":** Warren loses at club, racecourse; Anselm Manor in danger. Derby: Sandstone wins; Warren bets on Saint. Coronation Cup at Epsom: Saint beats Vulture (American owner, jockey crouched), Coralie, Avenger, Decoy Duck, Mermaid by a short head.

**Ch XVII "The Squire Overhears":** Felix confronts Warren in paddock; Warren strikes him. Felix tells Squire of "Mrs Warren". Squire gets card; Warren tears one up. Warren confesses to Irene; Irene reveals she knows; threatens to tell Squire; Warren threatens to sell Manor and leave.

**Ch XVIII "Tally-Ho!":** Ulick rides Random (borrowed from Irene via Eli) with Rushshire Hunt at Helton; Squire has gout, absent. James Bard (vet). Hunt meet at Hazelwell; run to Brecon Wood, Tone river, fox heads for Glen church. Warren on grey Irish horse; dares Ulick to follow him over churchyard wall; Ulick refuses.

**Ch XIX "A Fatal Leap":** Warren jumps churchyard wall; grey falls onto Harewood's vault slab; Warren's neck broken (dies). Squire and Irene arrive; Irene faints on Warren's body. Warren buried at Anselm church. Janet returns to Eli; confirms Warren ran away with her.

**Ch XX "Perfect Harmony":** A year after; Ulick proposes to Irene at Hazelwell on anniversary night. Married in summer; abroad; then Anselm Manor. Janet becomes Irene's lady's maid when Mary Marley and Bob Heather marry. Felix flees country. Grandson Ulick born on anniversary day; Saint's stud career.

---

## Quick facts list
- Book 1 names: Jim Dennis, Willie, Sal, Dr Tom Sheridan, Ned Glenn, Doonan, Machinson, Abe Dalton, Rodney Shaw, Benjamin Nix, Alec Beg, Maud Dennis, Seth Sharp, King Charlie, Silas Dixon, Adye Dauntsey, Molly Corbold, Chris Shaw, Grey Bird, Neptune, Seahorse, Bess (mare), Baalim (dog), Aaron Hyam, Ben Madsley, Jackson, Hurley, Jack Ashton, Defiance, Bung Bung.
- Book 2 names: Redmond Maynard, Irene Courtly/Carstone, Warren Courtly, Ulick Maynard, Eli Todd, Janet Todd, Bersak, Random, Honeysuckle, Rupert, Bob Heather, Mary Marley, Martha Dixon, Felix Hoffman, Mrs Hoffman, Fred May, Ben Sprig, Dr Harding, James Bard, Sam Lane, Conrad Rush, Vulture, Coralie, Sandstone, Saint, Kit Cat, Pinkerton, Janet's alias "Mrs Warren".
- Dates: Book 1 "Settling Day" = Jim's oath; Book 2 anniversary = night Ulick left (New Year's Eve/January reference; Ulick left on a night in winter).
